_readme: The forward plan for Cosmos after session 1. Each numbered session is scoped to one sitting and ends with something the user can play or use. 'backlog' holds real, session-sized ideas that are not scheduled yet; keep adding to it. A session that finds a better order says so in its own manifest and edits this file.
what_the_user_asked_for: A cool astronomy, galaxy and solar-system map plus gravity games: all of a sandbox, orbit puzzles, a Kerbal-style spaceflight sim (3D), an arcade shooter, and a music visualizer built both into Cosmos and as PulseForge scenes. The real galaxy map starts from HYG, and a Gaia layer comes later on the AN3 drive. Session 1 was the map and the sandbox.
rules_that_hold_for_every_session: Adding a mode is one folder under static/modes with a mode.json; nothing else lists modes.
Adding a body, level, part or preset is one JSON file in its folder, never a new hardcoded list.
Physics and orbital maths live in static/core, stay DOM-free and are tested with node --test before any drawing is built on them.
Large data goes on AN3 (/run/media/ejb/AN3/Cosmos) with a graceful fallback when the drive is out; ask before any download over about 50 MB.
When the honest simulation looks wrong, improve the drawing, not the physics.
Every mode works fullscreen (shared forge_chrome.js, f key) and Esc backs out one level.

session_2.title: Orbit puzzles
session_2.why: The sandbox proves the engine; puzzles give it goals. Slingshot puzzles teach real orbital intuition, and the engine's predict() already draws a probe's future path.

user_decisions_2026-09-16._note: The user answered 15 design questions before this session was built. These override anything older in this block. They said no more questions after these, so build from them.
user_decisions_2026-09-16.view: 3D, like the map (Three.js). NOT 2D like the sandbox.
user_decisions_2026-09-16.launch_controls: Both: drag to aim, plus number fields for speed and angle to fine-tune.
user_decisions_2026-09-16.burns: Pure launches in early levels; later levels give a small fuel budget for mid-flight burns.
user_decisions_2026-09-16.path_preview: Full predicted path on early levels, shortening as levels get harder.
user_decisions_2026-09-16.realism: Made-up toy systems early; late levels use real bodies from data/bodies.
user_decisions_2026-09-16.levels: 10 hand-made levels plus an endless mode of generated levels, each checked as solvable before it is shown.
user_decisions_2026-09-16.stars: A mix: one star for finishing, one for par fuel or speed, one for a bonus goal.
user_decisions_2026-09-16.goal_types: Reach a moving planet, settle into an orbit, pass waypoints in order, land on a body, and also an open 'just explore the galaxy' level with no goal to fail.
user_decisions_2026-09-16.hazards: Crashing into bodies, black holes, asteroid fields, and out of bounds. Set out of bounds VERY far away: the user wants to try long shots.
user_decisions_2026-09-16.after_failure: Instant retry with the previous attempts' paths drawn faintly (ghosts).
user_decisions_2026-09-16.teaching: A short plain-language caption per level on the real orbital idea it uses.
user_decisions_2026-09-16.sound: A small set (launch, burn, crash, win) as JSON recipes in ~/ForgeGameData/sounds, no audio files.
user_decisions_2026-09-16.progress_saving: A JSON file in ~/ForgeGameData/cosmos/ through the backend, not localStorage.

session_2.consequence_of_3d: static/core/nbody.js is 2D. 3D puzzles need a 3D n-body integrator with predict() in static/core first, tested under node like nbody.js. Pulling that forward is overlap with session 7's orbit3d.js, so build it to be reused there.
do: static/core: a 3D n-body integrator with prediction, DOM-free, node tests for energy conservation and a reference solution per level.
static/modes/puzzles/ in Three.js with a level select, star ratings, ghosts of past attempts and per-level captions.

Levels as JSON in ~/ForgeGameData/cosmos/levels/*.json: bodies, a launch point, allowed launch speed and angle range, a goal (moving target, orbit capture, waypoints, landing, or none for explore), hazards, a fuel budget and a very large bounds radius.
Ten hand-made levels climbing from a straight shot to a double gravity assist, plus an endless generator that only serves levels its own solver can finish.
Backend endpoints to read and write puzzle progress in ~/ForgeGameData/cosmos/, with pytest.
Sound recipes in ~/ForgeGameData/sounds.
session_2.status: Done in session 2 (2026-09-16). See manifests/session-02.json for what was built, verified and left.
session_2.level_order_as_built: Levels 1-7 are made-up systems, 8-10 real bodies: 1 First light, 2 Lead the target, 3 Around the corner, 4 Slingshot, 5 Ring road, 6 Event horizon, 7 Parking orbit (first burns), 8 Moonfall (land on the real Moon), 9 Belt run (real Mars to a Jupiter orbit), 10 Grand tour (real Jupiter slingshot to Saturn). Parking orbit moved from 4 to 7 so burns arrive late, as the user chose.
session_2.endless_note: Endless levels use reach and ring goals only, because they are proven solvable with a launch and no burns. Orbit and landing goals live in the hand-made levels.

session_3.title: Arcade gravity shooter
session_3.why: The fast, fun mode. Spacewar with real gravity wells: bullets and ships both fall toward the star.
do: static/modes/shooter/: one or two players on one keyboard, thrust and turn, shots as particles, respawn, a score limit.
Arenas as JSON (star mass, extra planets, wraparound or bounded).
Sounds through shared/forge_sound.js recipes in ~/ForgeGameData/sounds, not audio files.
A simple computer opponent that aims using predict().

session_4.title: Live music visualizer mode
session_4.why: The user asked for a space visualizer in Cosmos itself. The galaxy model, star shader and n-body particles are already the visual vocabulary.
do: static/modes/visualizer/: open an audio file (stays in the browser; nothing uploaded), a Web Audio AnalyserNode driving scenes.

Scenes as small modules listed by a scenes.json in the mode folder: galaxy pulse (arms brighten on bass), orbit rings (planets spin with tempo), nebula particles (n-body dust thrown by transients), starfield warp.
Test whether WebKitGTK inside Forge allows getUserMedia for system or monitor audio. If it does not, say so plainly in the mode and the manifest; do not fake it.
explicitly_not: No video export here; that is PulseForge's job (session 5)

session_5.title: Cosmos scenes for PulseForge
session_5.why: The user wants the same space visuals exportable as music videos, and PulseForge already renders and muxes.
do: pulseforge/scenes/cosmos_galaxy.py and cosmos_orbits.py following that app's contract: SCENE metadata plus frames(ctx) yielding (H, W, 3) uint8 frames, and one line each in scenes/registry.py _MODULES.
Port only the maths needed (galaxy model, star colour) to numpy; do not import the browser code.
Use the scene's music analysis (beats, sections) the way aurora.py does.
Render a 10-second test clip and look at frames before calling it done.
explicitly_not: Do not change PulseForge's render pipeline
prerequisites: session_4 is useful for agreeing the look, but not required

session_6.title: 3D spaceflight sim, part 1: rockets from parts
session_6.why: The Kerbal-style sim is the biggest piece, so it gets four sessions. Building a rocket comes first because every later part needs a vehicle with mass, thrust and stages.
do: static/core/rocket.js: parts from ~/ForgeGameData/cosmos/parts/*.json (mass dry and wet, thrust, Isp, drag area, size), stacking, stages, and delta-v per stage by the rocket equation, with node tests.
static/modes/flight/ builder screen in Three.js: stack parts vertically, see mass, thrust-to-weight and delta-v update live.
explicitly_not: No radial or symmetry attachment yet

session_7.title: 3D spaceflight sim, part 2: flight in one gravity well
session_7.why: Launch to orbit around one body is the core loop.
do: static/core/orbit3d.js: state vectors <-> Keplerian elements, 3D integration with thrust, time warp that switches to on-rails Kepler propagation when not thrusting.
Flight view: chase camera, navball-style attitude readout, apoapsis/periapsis markers, the orbit line.
Bodies come from data/bodies with real radii and GM, optionally scaled down (a 'kerbal scale' setting) because real Earth orbit is slow to reach.

session_8.title: 3D spaceflight sim, part 3: spheres of influence and manoeuvre nodes
session_8.why: Going to the Moon and to other planets.
do: Patched conics: sphere-of-influence changes, planned manoeuvre nodes with a predicted trajectory, transfer windows using the real ephemeris.

session_9.title: 3D spaceflight sim, part 4: atmosphere, landing and docking
do: An exponential atmosphere with drag and heating for bodies that have one (data in body JSON), landing legs and touchdown speed, a docking target with relative-velocity readouts.

session_10.title: Gaia layer on AN3
session_10.why: The user asked for a realistic star map of the galaxy, put on AN3 if too big. HYG is only the Sun's neighbourhood.
do: Measure the real download size first and ask the user before pulling anything (their disk memory says so).
A tool that builds a Gaia DR3 subset (for example, G < 16 with good parallax) into distance-sorted chunks on AN3, plus a small cache copy of the brightest part.
Streaming in the map: load chunks by camera distance, same star shader.
explicitly_not: Never write the chunks to the internal disk except the small cache

backlog.title: Constellation lines and a sky view from Earth
backlog.why: Standing on Earth looking up is the most familiar view of the stars; HYG already has constellation membership.

backlog.title: Exoplanet systems
backlog.why: Known planets around nearby stars, from the NASA Exoplanet Archive, shown when you fly to a star.

backlog.title: Comets and asteroids
backlog.why: Named comets and the brightest asteroids from JPL SBDB as more body files, plus an asteroid-belt particle layer in the map.

backlog.title: Eclipse and conjunction finder
backlog.why: Search the ephemeris for eclipses and planet alignments, then fly the camera there at that moment.

backlog.title: Sandbox level editor for puzzles
backlog.why: Make puzzle levels by placing things in the sandbox and marking a target.

backlog.title: Barnes-Hut gravity for massive swarms
backlog.why: Let particles pull on each other for real galaxy formation, which needs O(n log n) gravity and probably a Web Worker.

backlog.title: Guided tours
backlog.why: Scripted camera flights with captions: scale of the universe, Voyager's route, where the Sun goes in 250 million years.

backlog.title: Spacecraft trajectories
backlog.why: Voyager, New Horizons and JWST paths from JPL Horizons vectors, drawn in the map for their real dates.

backlog.title: Puzzle tuning from real play
backlog.why: Every level has a solver-found reference and 3 achievable stars, but nobody has played them. Pars, bonus thresholds, launch-speed ranges and preview lengths should be tuned from the user's first tries.

backlog.title: Orbit and landing goals in endless mode
backlog.why: The generator only makes reach and ring levels; it could build capture and landing levels with the solver's braking autopilot as proof.
